spans.text: Exolunar vessels assailed by the treacherous inhabitants and environments of deep space often meet their untimely demise, being marooned with their crew still alive while they drift helplessly to their doom. In some rare cases, a convergence of astral energies, psychic resonance from dying or dead crew and passengers, or a misuse of arcane techniques can breathe new life into a dying vessel, causing it to come to life as a possessed object. These ships may revive their old crew as well, as undead spirits or grafted automatons, but they have a will of their own and usually seek to take revenge on other ships not yet liberated from their roles.

Animated vessels come in many sizes, and are somewhat supernatural in their presentation. They can undergo self-repair, taking in surrounding elements and materials to stitch their hulls together and create new fuel and ammunition. This process leaves them with a unique construction, and as more time passes they only become more distinct. They are aggressive toward other exolunar vessels, but often naturally collaborate with other animated vessels of the same type.
The construct does not require air, food, or water to survive.

“Living ships can serve as allies to their would-be crews, or can become no better than beasts themselves. I wonder what it’s like to have the wants of such a vessel? I hunger, yearn, and grow bored... so a living astradeck experience those sorts of desires? It must be horrible to have such a singular purpose and existence.”
